topics.display_title: The Beginnings of European Settlements (Portuguese → Dutch → English → French)

panels.title: Scope: contact, settlement and empire are different stages
ascii_lines: CAPE ROUTE 1498 -> repeated trade -> factory by Indian permission
FACTORY -> fortified settlement -> presidency / regional coordination
POSSIBLE COMPANY-STATE -> additionally needs finance, army, allies, victory and revenue
ANTI-TELEOLOGY -> neither a European charter nor the first voyage made conquest inevitable.
MUST REMEMBER: The maritime sequence runs through the Portuguese arrival in 1498 and Goa in
1510, the English Company charter of 1600, the Dutch VOC of 1602 and the French Company of
source_references: 01. Scope: five stages, not one inevitable conquest

panels.title: Indian Ocean setting and mercantilist armed commerce
ascii_lines: PRE-1498 -> monsoon routes + Asian merchants + Indian ports and manufactures
MERCANTILISM -> chartered monopoly seeks bullion, commodities and protected markets
ARMED COMMERCE -> ship cannon + fort + pass + diplomacy + corporate privilege
LIMIT -> Europeans entered an existing oceanic economy; older circuits did not disappear.
source_references: 02. Maritime background: the Indian Ocean before the Europeans
21. Commodities, bullion and the port-hinterland network

panels.title: Portuguese Estado da India and cartaz
ascii_lines: 1498 CALICUT -> 1505 Estado administration -> GOA captured 1510 / capital 1530
ESTADO -> Crown + viceroy/governor + fleet + forts + royal factories
CARTAZ -> coerced shipping pass; fortified nodes at Goa, Cochin, Diu and Daman
LIMIT -> nodal and contested control, never a complete monopoly of Indian Ocean trade.
source_references: 05. Portuguese arrival and the Estado da India
06. Cartaz, naval power, diplomacy and conflict

panels.title: Portuguese cultural transfer and bounded Goa heritage
ascii_lines: XAVIER -> Goa 1542; founding Jesuit companion; died off China, remains at Bom Jesus
GOA PRESS 1556 | INQUISITION 1560 -> mission, print, coercion and accommodation coexist
CROPS -> papaya, pineapple and guava through Portuguese networks; no exact transfer year
UNESCO -> Indo-Portuguese forms + local adaptation; threats include damp, weathering, termites.
source_references: 07. Portuguese trade, mission, printing, crops and cultural exchange

panels.title: Dutch VOC: commercial strength, India inside an Asian portfolio
ascii_lines: VOC 1602 -> joint-stock capital + treaty, war and fortification powers
INDIAN NODES -> Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nagapattinam, Surat, Chinsura and Cochin
PRIORITY -> Indian textiles finance an Indonesia-centred spice and intra-Asian portfolio
CHECKS -> Colachel 1741 / Bedara 1759; political retreat did not instantly end trade.
source_references: 09. Dutch VOC: structure, Indian bases and Indonesian priority
10. Why Dutch power in India remained commercial

panels.title: English entry: charter, naval credibility and Mughal permission
ascii_lines: EIC CHARTER 1600 -> corporate monopoly in English law, not Indian sovereignty
SWALLY 1612 -> naval credibility alters Mughal bargaining
SURAT FACTORY 1613 -> licensed depot; ROE 1615-19 -> privileges confirmed
CHILD'S WAR 1686-90 -> Mughal victory proves early Company weakness and contingency.
source_references: 11. English EIC foundation, early voyages and Mughal diplomacy
12. Surat and the first English factory network

panels.title: English fortified settlement chain
ascii_lines: MASULIPATNAM 1611 -> MADRAS lease 1639 -> Fort St George from 1640
BOMBAY -> Portuguese possession -> Crown 1661 -> Company 1668 -> presidency HQ 1687
BENGAL -> Hugli / Kasimbazar -> three-village Calcutta hub -> 1698 zamindari -> 1717 farman
CAUTION -> Job Charnock is a conventional association, not an uncontested sole founder.
source_references: 13. Coromandel chain: Masulipatnam, Madras and Fort St George
14. Bombay: Crown transfer, harbour geography and presidency shift
15. Bengal factories, Calcutta and the pre-Plassey boundary

panels.title: Institutional vocabulary that prevents category errors
ascii_lines: CHARTER -> home sovereign creates company | FARMAN -> Indian sovereign grants privilege
FACTORY -> depot + factors | FORT -> defended enclave, not automatic hinterland rule
PRESIDENCY -> regional council coordinating factories, fleets, defence and diplomacy
COMPANY-STATE -> enforceable war, justice, taxation and territory; capacity must match claim.
source_references: 16. Charter, farman, factory, fort and presidency: terminology that decides marks

panels.title: French Compagnie and Indian settlement chain
ascii_lines: COMPAGNIE DES INDES 1664 -> Colbert / Louis XIV state-backed monopoly
SURAT 1668 -> MASULIPATNAM 1669 -> PONDICHERRY 1673-74 -> CHANDERNAGORE c.1690-92
DUPLEIX -> trade + trained troops + claimant politics; Indian allies retain their own aims
LIMIT -> finance, naval continuity and home-state priorities constrain French intervention.
source_references: 17. French Compagnie des Indes and the settlement chain
18. Dupleix and the bounded bridge to Carnatic rivalry

panels.title: Carnatic conclusion: European rivalry becomes Indian politics
ascii_lines: FIRST WAR 1746-48 -> French take Madras -> Aix-la-Chapelle restores it
SECOND 1749-54 -> Carnatic / Hyderabad claimants + Arcot -> Dupleix recalled
THIRD 1756-63 -> Seven Years' War -> WANDIWASH 1760 breaks French field power
PARIS 1763 -> factories survive, political ambition checked; no single-cause English victory.
CLOSE DISTINCTION: A factory was a trading station, not automatically territorial sovereignty;
cartaz, naval force, diplomacy, farmans and fortified settlements had different
legal-political effects.
source_references: 18. Dupleix and the bounded bridge to Carnatic rivalry
25. Why the English gained relative advantage - without teleology

panels.title: Indian agency and the port-hinterland engine
ascii_lines: RULERS -> grant, revise, resist and use rival companies against one another
MERCHANTS / BANKERS / DUBASHES -> credit, brokerage, customs and information
WEAVERS / ARTISANS / SHIPBUILDERS / LABOUR -> make commercial settlements viable
ASYMMETRY -> agency was real but unequal; forts still depended on surrounding Indian society.
EVIDENCE LIMIT: European archives privilege company aims; Indian merchants, rulers, port
ecologies and Asian commercial rivals are necessary evidence against a Europe-only
inevitability story.
source_references: 20. Indian rulers, merchants, brokers, artisans and port communities
21. Commodities, bullion and the port-hinterland network
